name: Apple notarization and app review gates
plain: Apple scans apps outside the App Store before install in the EU and Japan.
meaning: Apps distributed through alternative marketplaces or the web still pass Apple checks for malware and platform rules. The checks do not review content.

android.permission: None; Play Protect scanning of sideloaded apps
android.prompt_ui: Play Protect warning for unknown apps
android.api_surface: Play Protect live threat detection, Play Integrity
android.note: Android has no mandatory pre install review for sideloaded apps.

ios.note: Required for EU marketplace and web apps and for Japan marketplaces.

limits.headline: Can install apps from outside the App Store in the EU and Japan after Apple checks
limits.user_action: You install a marketplace or web app and see a sheet with the developer's name
can: Install apps that Apple has notarized on iPhone in the EU
Show the notarized developer in the install sheet
Install through approved marketplaces in Japan
cannot: Install an unchecked app on iPhone in these regions
Skip the check for marketplaces or web apps
Get this on Android, which has no required review for side loaded apps; Play Protect only warns
limits.differs: Apple checks apps outside the App Store in the EU and Japan. Android has no required review for side loaded apps.

story.what_it_is: Apple scans apps in the EU and Japan for malware before they can be installed from outside the App Store.

marketing.name: Notarization for iOS apps in the EU
marketing.pitch: Apple describes notarization as a check for malware and platform rules for apps distributed outside the App Store in the EU.

story.for_you: You install an app from a web page or an alternative store, and a system screen shows the developer's name. The app has already passed Apple's basic safety check.
story.for_makers: Makers who distribute outside the App Store still need Apple's approval of the file. Apple says it checks for malware and rules, not content.

use_cases.example: A studio releases a game on its own site and gets it notarized first.
An alternative store lists apps that each passed notarization.
A malware author finds it harder to ship through a fake store.
A company sends a private app to its staff with the check done.
A small team treats the check as a new step in its release process.
A social app released outside the main store still goes through it.
A bank app avoids fake copies with the developer name shown at install.

story.android_note: Android has no mandatory check for sideloaded apps beyond Play Protect warnings.
story.ios_note: Required for EU marketplaces and web apps and for Japan marketplaces.

history.change: Notarization for iOS apps outside the App Store
